messages:
maya: FYI — AcmeBank (dedicated pool-3) is hitting p99 tails & intermittent 503s since ~2026-03-17 17:00 UTC. CS escalated to P1. Need owners and short workaround timeline. Alert: https://redwood.inc/alerts/ACME-502-p99

jonathan: looking. can you paste the most recent logs and the alert context?

maya: logs snippet below (redacted):
```
[17:08:12] queue_wait_ms=1243 gid=pool-3 req_id=... status=timeout
[17:08:13] redis: slowcmd 1200ms key=kvcache:... 
[17:08:14] inference: 503 downstream capacity exhausted
```
also saw auth 401 spikes for a subset of requests.

sara: routing fallback owner here. Quick option: enable model fallback to quantized-4bit variant for pool-3. This avoids heavy kernel paths. Need ~15-20m to flip + validate canary. I'll own verification.

sara: config change (canary):
```
PATCH /api/admin/pools/3/config
{ "enable_model_fallback": true, "fallback_model": "gptx-quant-4b" }
```

phil: I have a reduce-queue-lock patch in branch fix/queue-lock (PR #439). It reduces dequeuing contention. Estimate ~2h for review + canary rollout. Can pair with infra.

tess: note: enabling fallback for AcmeBank requires a VPC egress route to the quant-model endpoints (customer private routing). Infra-side change is ~30m. I can take it but need coordination window.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled by phil at 1769452610 for branch fix/queue-lock -> pool-3-canary.

maya: Proposed plan:
- owners: sara (model fallback), tess (VPC egress), phil (hotfix PR)
- immediate (0-30m): sara flips fallback + tess applies VPC egress change
- short-term (2h): phil canary deploys hotfix, monitor p99 and error rate
- goal: reduce p99 below SLA threshold within 2h, otherwise rollback & escalate to infra oncall.
I'll update CS with owners and ETA.

jonathan: I'll watch metrics/dashboards and mute noisy alerts. ping me if canary shows regressions. :eyes:

sara: starting fallback canary now, will post status in ~10m.

phil: pushing PR for review, requesting @jonathan for quick LGTM.

maya: thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
